It's alright, as long as you're extremely realistic about the state of the game. What you get for free is time-gated progression grinding with constant reminders of how much money you COULD be spending on the game, as well as how much better everyone who spends money on the game performs in every game mode compared to you.

Combat is mostly carried out on auto mode at 2x speed except for content where manual control is required (arena, whatever your current highest dungeon boss floor is). Everything is managed primarily through teambuilding (champion and gear selection). Endless grinding is required to pull the right champions, tier them up, unlock their skills, get the right gear pieces with the right set bonus and the right rarity and right number of stars and then hope that the main stats and substats are not only the ones you need but also rolled on the higher end of the scale, and

If you're a beginner player, it's way too much work to start a new game using Steam.  Not being able to take advantage of CC links puts you at a disadvantage if you just started a new account on their native app and get two legendary champs and a few epics.  By using the CC link and a beginner code gives you the two legendary champs while leveling up will award you with 3 epics.
In terms of overall gameplay, if you like grinding dungeons to level up champs and collecting champs then this is a game for you.  Having better gear is what will set you apart and make your account progress over roadblocks.  So the dungeon grind is where you will spend a ton of energy. 
There have been many QOL improvements over the years and it's getting better.  I don't like the energy cap of 130 and hopefully that changes in the future.

reviews.title: Genuinely Good Game But…
reviews.text:
The game is great, it’s fun, absorbing, and full. The game is easy to pick up and has a rewarding story if you like 100% it. However, as good as the game is I have a few grievances. 1, this game is extremely grindy and it’s hard to get good characters early on without getting promo codes. 2, after level 20 it gets insanely hard to level up so it locks good leveling rewards behind a brick wall of grinding. 3, pvp is incredibly unbalanced, my team of one legendary and 3 rares is constantly put up against teams comprising of all level 60 legendaries in silver one. 4, I understand that this is a mobile game and it makes its money off in game packs, but getting any legendaries is basically locked behind a pay wall, so people with money to throw around get stacked teams early game. With less monetization a few leveling tweaks and pvp balancing this game would easily be 5 stars.

reviews.title: Spend or Stall
reviews.text:
I wanted to enjoy RAID because the gameplay, champion designs, and overall presentation are genuinely good. Unfortunately, the summoning system completely ruins the experience.
The summon rates are incredibly low, and it feels like you’re constantly opening shards only to get duplicate rares or champions you’ll never use. The biggest issue is Mythical champions. While they’re technically obtainable for free, in reality they feel locked behind spending money because Primal Shards are so scarce for free-to-play players. The game heavily encourages buying crystals and shard packs if you actually want a realistic chance at getting one. Primal Shards are the only way to summon Mythical champions, with very low base odds. One of if not the worse rates in any game of this caliber.
